title: Deciding Officials, Standard of Review and Decision Goals — Decision Reviews and Appeals
content:
**Decision Reviews and Appeals — reference card: who decides, how, and how long**

The table records for each of the six lanes of Decision Reviews and Appeals who decides the request, whether the review is a new look that gives no deference to the earlier decision, whether the person who made the earlier decision may decide it, what a Veterans Law Judge reviews on a Board docket, VA's published average-days goal for completing a request, whether a pre-decisional duty-to-assist error found in the lane is returned to the regional office for correction, and whether a returned issue is readjudicated with priority.

| Lane | Decided by | New look, no deference to the earlier decision | Earlier decision-maker may decide | What the Veterans Law Judge reviews | Published average-days goal (calendar days) | Duty-to-assist error returned to the regional office | Returned issue readjudicated with priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supplemental Claim | A claims adjudicator | Yes | No | Not applicable | 125 | No | Yes |
| Higher-Level Review | A senior reviewer | Yes | No | Not applicable | 125 | Yes | Yes |
| Higher-Level Review with Informal Conference | A senior reviewer | Yes | No | Not applicable | 125 | Yes | Yes |
| Board Appeal - Direct Review Docket | A Veterans Law Judge | Yes | No | The record as it stood at the agency decision | 365 | Yes | Yes |
| Board Appeal - Evidence Submission Docket | A Veterans Law Judge | Yes | No | The record plus evidence received within the docket's window | 550 | Yes | Yes |
| Board Appeal - Hearing Docket | A Veterans Law Judge | Yes | No | The record plus the hearing testimony and evidence received within the docket's window | 730 | Yes | Yes |

**Reading the card by row**

- *Deciding official.* The Supplemental Claim lane is decided by a claims adjudicator, both Higher-Level Review lanes by a senior reviewer, and all three Board dockets by a Veterans Law Judge.
- *Standard of review.* Every lane gives a new look with no deference to the earlier decision, and in no lane may the person who made the earlier decision decide the review.
- *Scope on the Board dockets.* The Direct Review Docket is confined to the record as it stood at the agency decision; the Evidence Submission Docket adds evidence received within its window; the Hearing Docket adds hearing testimony as well as evidence received within its window.
- *Goals.* The goal is a published average in calendar days: 125 for the three regional office lanes, 365 for the Direct Review Docket, 550 for the Evidence Submission Docket and 730 for the Hearing Docket. The Hearing Docket goal of 730 days is twice the Direct Review Docket goal of 365 days.
- *Duty-to-assist errors.* A pre-decisional duty-to-assist error found in either Higher-Level Review lane or on any Board docket is returned to the regional office for correction; the Supplemental Claim lane is shown as not returning such an error. In every lane, a returned issue is readjudicated with priority.

**Hypothetical comparison.** A claimant weighing the Direct Review Docket against the Hearing Docket for one issue would find on this card that both are decided by a Veterans Law Judge with no deference to the earlier decision, that the Direct Review Docket looks only at the record as it stood at the agency decision while the Hearing Docket adds testimony and window evidence, and that the published average-days goals are 365 and 730 calendar days respectively.
